status: exploratory (re-run of E001's pre-registered criterion against the corrected scoring)
why: E001 evaluated scoring 0.1.0 and found no information beyond trivial baselines at any horizon. Scoring 0.2.0 (2026-09-22) fixed a real flaw in that object: history was counted in rows, so 9.26% of hours were scored on windows that silently spanned more time than they claimed (E016). The live system now runs 0.2.0, so the baseline evaluation must be restated for the thing that is actually running. This is a re-run of an existing question against a corrected input -- not a new hypothesis, and not a second attempt at a result that was not liked.
hypothesis: Scoring 0.2.0 (technical categories only; news absent in replay) contains predictive information beyond trivial baselines at at least one horizon among 1h, 6h, 24h, 72h, 168h.
acceptance_criterion: COPIED VERBATIM FROM E001, unchanged, so the two are comparable: For a horizon to count as 'information present': (a) the system's edge (mean forward return after BUY minus after SELL) is positive with a block-bootstrap 95% interval excluding zero in BOTH exploration and validation, AND (b) its three-class balanced accuracy (fixed 0.5% band) exceeds every trivial baseline's in BOTH periods. Anything less is reported as 'no evidence of information beyond baselines' for that horizon. No horizon is chosen as primary from this experiment alone.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A horizon meeting both parts of the criterion under 0.2.0 that failed under 0.1.0 would mean the gap flaw had been masking a real signal -- a genuinely new finding, to be reported as such and then re-tested, never adopted from one run. The expected outcome is that the conclusion is unchanged: 0.2.0 differs from 0.1.0 on only 9.26% of hours, and there it REMOVES inputs rather than adding information. A worse result is equally possible and equally publishable: on those hours the system now abstains, so its remaining acted hours are a different, smaller sample.
method: agent/research/evaluate.py, unchanged, on the cached scoring-0.2.0 replay of the same snapshot and the same 68,619 hours (2017-08-27 -> 2025-06-30; the holdout is not read). Same five horizons, same binary and three-class labels, same trivial baselines (always-HOLD, random with the system's own signal mix, momentum 24h, MA 200h, majority), same circular block bootstrap (block = max(48, 2H), 500 resamples), same per-year and per-regime slices, same confidence-reliability tables.

comparison_targets_from_E001.confidence: stated 0.68-0.91, observed 0.42-0.50 in every bucket; ECE 0.36-0.39
comparison_targets_from_E001.verdict: criterion not met at any horizon

metrics.tool: agent/research/compare_baselines.py (re-applies E001 criterion to both result files)

balanced_accuracy_3class_vs_best_baselin.1h: 0.354 vs 0.334 (expl), 0.350 vs 0.339 (vali) -- above in both, but criterion (a) fails

metrics.acted_direction_accuracy: 0.475-0.493 (0.2.0) vs the majority baseline 0.508-0.561 -- still below always-UP at every horizon and period
metrics.acted_share: 72% exploration (was 73% under 0.1.0): the hours that lost every category now fall to HOLD
metrics.confidence_reliability: ECE 0.357-0.380, hit rate 0.475-0.493 whatever confidence was stated -- unchanged and still uninformative
metrics.validation_period_identical: Every validation figure matches E001 to the digit, because all 28 Binance gaps fall in 2017-2021 and one stretch ending 2023-04: the validation period has no gap-affected hour, so 0.2.0 IS 0.1.0 there. An independent confirmation of E016.

results: CONCLUSION UNCHANGED: no evidence of information beyond trivial baselines at any of the five horizons, under the corrected scoring, by E001s own criterion applied to both result files. The validation period is numerically identical to E001 (it contains no gap-affected hours), so only the exploration period could move -- and it moved the way a correctness fix should. The one substantive change: at 6h the exploration edge under 0.1.0 was +0.092% with an interval that EXCLUDED zero [+0.002, +0.172]; under 0.2.0 it is +0.076% with an interval that INCLUDES zero [-0.011, +0.155]. That borderline half-signal was partly an artefact of hours scored across data holes. The same shrinkage appears at 24h (+0.184 -> +0.078), 72h (+0.747 -> +0.404) and 168h (+1.200 -> +0.611): every apparent exploration edge got smaller when the system stopped scoring hours it could not actually see. Nothing improved and nothing new appeared: acted-direction accuracy stays at 0.475-0.493 against a majority baseline of 0.508-0.561, and the confidence heuristic remains uninformative (ECE 0.36-0.38, hit rate ~0.48 at every stated level).
affected_design: The live system now runs scoring 0.2.0 and the baseline statement for it is this experiment; E001 remains the record for 0.1.0 and is not edited. No phase reopens: Phase 10 stays closed (there is still nothing to re-weight towards), E011s null stands, and the deliverable remains calibrated move-size uncertainty plus HOLD-heavy direction. One lesson recorded for future work: a borderline result that sits on the edge of its interval should be checked against data-quality flags before it is believed -- here the 6h exploration edge crossed zero once hours with holes in their window stopped being scored.
notes: E001 is not edited or superseded: it remains the record for scoring 0.1.0. This experiment is the record for 0.2.0. Both stay in the log, each naming its version, which is the entire reason the version stamps exist.
